story_candidates.title: AI physiotherapy in Portugal's health service: what the government says

ai_path.connection: Direct: AI tools that analyse and correct a patient's movements in real time, under permanent supervision by health professionals, in the national health service.
ai_path.places: Portugal's national health service (SNS), nine local health units, patients at home.

story_candidates.angle: The government's own news item says the national health service has an agreement with Sword Health to offer remote physiotherapy for common muscle and joint problems: a doctor prescribes it, a clinical team assesses the patient, equipment comes to the home, AI tools analyse and correct movements in real time under permanent supervision by health professionals, and it is free to users. Nine local health units signed protocols the same day to explore AI in triage, continued care and mental health. The 97 percent cut in the wait and 45 percent saving are the government's estimates, not measured results.
story_candidates.note: For journalist-portugal. Ready. Conditions: re-read the page yourself; one source, so attribute everything to the government ('the government says'); the 97 percent and 45 percent figures are estimates, say so; the page gives the date inconsistently (an event on 18 June, 'updated 24 June 2026', a photo caption saying 18 May): say 'June 2026, according to the page' and do not give a firmer date; 'available from next week' is relative to that page, so say what it said, not that the service is running now; the page does not mention the 'two years to ten days' hospital claim from the Center for Responsible AI interview (S67's update) and does not confirm it: do not link this service to the Center beyond saying Sword Health appears in both, and do not confirm that claim; no price or patient-count claims beyond the page; say plainly that AI tools correct movements and health professionals supervise; the AI connection (direct, 0 steps; the national health service, nine local health units, patients at home) goes in the data note; explain technical terms at first use; length follows the story (standing answer 92); categories Portugal and AI.

for_the_fact_checker.what: One official source with an inconsistent date; the figures are estimates; no independent check of the service's start, uptake or results was found.

The update repeats the chief executive's 'two years to ten days' claim as his; this government item does not confirm it (it gives only the 97 percent estimate). The reviewer may want one clause saying the government's own figure is an estimate of 97 percent.
